name: Pocong
description: An Indonesian and Malay ghost that takes the form of a body still wrapped in its Islamic burial shroud (kain kafan), said to arise when the shroud's knots are not untied at burial. Because the feet are bound, the pocong moves by hopping rather than walking.
origin: Pervasive across Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei, and Malay-speaking regions of Singapore and southern Thailand. Strongly associated with Javanese, Sundanese, and Malay Muslim communities.
